title: Claude Enterprise can now show a team what its token spend produced
friendlyTitle: Claude Enterprise can now show a team what its spending produced
summary: Anthropic made three Claude Enterprise tools generally available on 28 October: smart reports, in-app surveys, and pooled group budgets. A report takes a team, a date range, and the products to include, then samples transcripts and groups the work into workstreams. It shows spend, deliverables, and common friction, such as a missing connector or a failed tool call. Surveys ask what would break if Claude disappeared. A pooled budget is one monthly pot for a group, with a member limit still acting as a guardrail.
friendlySummary: On 28 October, Anthropic turned on three tools for Claude Enterprise. Smart reports look at a sample of a team's chats and sort the work into streams. Each stream shows what it cost, what it produced, and where it got stuck, such as a missing connection or a failed tool. Short surveys ask people what would break if Claude went away. A pooled budget is one monthly pot for a group, so one heavy user is less likely to hit a personal limit while others leave money unused.
whyItMatters: The useful part is the refusal to treat the report as a performance review. Anthropic says the reports are for adoption and investment planning, not for evaluating a person or making an employment decision. Availability still depends on the account. Organizations with a HIPAA setup or customer-managed encryption keys may not get every piece. If you pay for Claude by the team, this is the first built-in way to see which workflows are worth turning into a skill, and which ones are just expensive.
